transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I explain this in a way that makes sense, I really want to be helpful today. 

I'm mostly here because of a situation with my house. Everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure I'm dealing with is just normal paperwork and missed payments. And I know how that sounds, I really do. But... well, I don't want you to think badly of me, or think I'm making things up, but I just know that the bank, the loan servicer, and even some of the people at my job—I'm a supervisor at a retail store—have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

They keep showing me all these official-looking papers to make it seem like a normal financial thing, but no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve actually been seeing happen for almost two years now. I'm just trying to get it sorted out and hoping someone will finally listen. Is... is that the kind of thing I should be telling you?
Aside from what you've noticed about the paperwork and the people involved, have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you don't seem to hear or see?

No, no, nothing like that. I promise I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I know sometimes people who... well, people who struggle with things might have that happen, but that's really not me. I'm completely clear-headed. 

I just notice the real things happening around me, like the way they talk to each other or the strange coincidences with the mail. But my mind isn't playing tricks on me with sounds or visions or anything. I hope that makes sense? I really want to be clear that I'm just dealing with a very difficult, real situation, not... not losing my mind. Does that answer your question okay?

Before this situation with your house started about two years ago, would you say you generally trusted people—friends, coworkers, family—or have you always tended to suspect that others were trying to deceive or take advantage of you, even back in your teens or twenties?

Oh, no, I've always been a very trusting person. I really have. I mean, growing up, and in my twenties... I always gave people the benefit of the doubt. I've always tried to be the kind of person who gets along with everyone, you know? At work, I'm a supervisor, so I really have to trust my team, and I always thought we had a great relationship. 

I don't want you to think I'm some sort of... paranoid person who just goes around suspecting everyone all the time. That's not me at all. I've always valued my friendships and my family, and I've never had any reason to think they were out to get me. 

It's really just... this specific situation with the house and the bank. It's so out of character for my life, which is why it's been so hard to deal with. Before all this started, I was just a regular person going to work and paying my bills. I hope you can see that I'm generally a very reasonable, trusting person. Is that... does that help give you a better picture of what I'm like?

Aside from your concerns about the house situation, has your ability to function—like performing your job duties, managing daily tasks, or maintaining relationships—stayed the same over these two years, or have you noticed any decline in these areas?

Well, outside of the whole house thing, I... I'm doing really well, actually. I still get up every day and go to work, and I do a good job. I manage my team, I handle all the scheduling, I deal with the customer complaints... I take pride in my work, and I make sure I take care of myself, too. I don't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything like that, because I'm really not. 

It's just... the only time things get a little hard is when the house stuff creeps in. Like if I get a piece of mail that looks strange, or the bank calls, or if there's paperwork at my job that seems... connected to what they're doing with my house. That's when I get a little distracted, but only because I have to be careful, you know? But otherwise, my life is completely normal. I'm still functioning just fine. I hope that's what you were asking? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre delusional belief (a conspiracy involving the bank, loan servicer, and coworkers to force her out of her house) persisting for approximately two years. There are no hallucinations, no evidence of premorbid paranoid personality traits (she reports being generally trusting prior to onset), no negative symptoms, and functioning is well preserved outside the delusional system (continues to work effectively as a supervisor, manages daily tasks).
